RagShortTexts: Ottokar II's iron cavalry shattered Hungarian hosts at Kressenbrunn to secure Austria.

Variants.Content: Contesting the Babenberg inheritance of Austria and Styria, King Ottokar II of Bohemia confronted King Béla IV of Hungary. On July 12, 1260, at Kressenbrunn, Ottokar's iron cavalry charged across the Morava River, routing the multi-ethnic Hungarian-Cuman army and cementing Přemyslid dominance.
Ottokar wields Kutná Hora silver mines (Gold) and mail-clad knight regiments (Iron). Victory at Kressenbrunn forced Hungary to cede Styria, projecting Bohemian power toward the Adriatic sea.
Across Morava gravel shoals, Cuman horse arrows skated off Bohemian plate coats. When Ottokar's lance wedges plunged through the shallows, the Hungarian line dissolved into a panicked stampede.
